description: Aenfinite is a team of curious builders exploring how our planet is changing. We aim to turn NASA Earth data into an interactive global tool that helps people discover, compare, and understand environmental trends. Our interests span coding, design, AI, and storytelling. We're looking for teammates with skills in web development, data analysis, Earth science, statistics, and visualization. Join us to turn open data into discoveries that matter.
summary: TerraSleuth AI is an environmental anomaly detection tool that flags months when Earth’s signals behave unusually together. It uses seven monthly inputs: NASA GPM IMERG rainfall, GLDAS soil water and evaporation, MODIS NDVI vegetation greenness, air temperature, and the ENSO and IOD climate indices. These become 18 engineered features, including seasonal anomalies, lagged “environmental memory”, year-over-year change and cross-signal combinations such as rain without a soil-water response. Two Isolation Forests, one pooled and one regional with 300 trees each, rank how unusual each month is. The score is a review aid, not a damage, cause or forecast claim. Trend estimation is kept separate, using autocorrelation-aware statistics. Our current development run covers one region in Sindh, Pakistan. TerraSleuth helps students and analysts decide which months deserve closer investigation using open NASA data.
details:
TerraSleuth AI is an interactive “Earth Detective” web platform that helps students, educators, citizen scientists and researchers investigate environmental questions with real NASA and NOAA data. One example question: can a region get heavier monsoon rain while losing dry-season soil moisture? The app removes the seasonal cycle, compares related signals, and highlights months where signals behave unusually together. It shows evidence, units, sources and uncertainty with every result.

How it works

  • Data: About 25 years (2000 to 2025) of monthly data from NASA GPM IMERG V07 (rainfall), GLDAS Noah 2.1 (modeled soil water and evaporation), Terra MODIS MOD13C2 (NDVI, with quality-flag screening), and MERRA-2 (air temperature). It adds NOAA PSL ENSO (Niño 3.4) and Indian Ocean Dipole indices. NASA GIBS satellite layers and NASA POWER point weather power the globe and map views. [Add NOAA GHCN-Daily only if station comparison actually runs.]
  • Features: Standardized seasonal anomalies, plus 18 engineered features. These cover 1, 3, 6 and 12-month memory, year-over-year change, lagged climate indices, and cross-signal coupling measures such as rain without a soil-water response.
  • ML: Two unsupervised Isolation Forests of 300 trees each, one pooled and one regional, with robust scaling. They rank how unusual each month is, with no anomaly labels needed.
  • Statistics: A separate trend pipeline, using regression with calendar-month effects and autocorrelation-robust errors, plus a Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall test. [Confirm which multiple-testing correction the code uses: Benjamini-Hochberg here, but Bonferroni in your validation spec.]
  • Honest outputs: When valid coverage is too low, the app returns “insufficient data” or “inconclusive” instead of guessing.

Benefits
It separates seasonal noise from real change, and it keeps observed, satellite-retrieved and model-based data clearly labeled. Every chart has downloadable CSV evidence with source, version, units and quality rules. It runs in a normal browser, and the backend sends light JSON and charts so it works on low-end devices.

Intended impact

  • Younger learners (ages 8 to 13): Guided mode with simple language, a step-by-step tour and read-aloud.
  • Older students: Explorer mode with multi-year series, two-location comparison, and raw, anomaly and trend views.
  • Communities and planners: Evidence from satellites for local weather and land questions.

Tools: TypeScript, Next.js 15, React 18, globe.gl, Three.js, Leaflet. Backend uses Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, scikit-learn, statsmodels, SciPy, NumPy, pandas, SQLite job queue. Data access uses NASA Earthaccess/CMR and GIBS. The AI assistant uses the Google Gemini API.

Creativity: The dual-mode interface, the detective-style investigation flow, and live satellite layers on a 3D globe.

Limitations and status: The anomaly score is a ranking aid for review. It is not a probability of flood, drought or damage, and paired trends do not prove a cause. Our current ML run covers one development region in Sindh, and broader validation is still in progress. [If you have measured results, state them here with how you measured them.]
